en: The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of Śrī Vidyāraṇya
The great yogi Vidyāraṇya, the illuminator of the Great Vidyā;
the restorer of Śrīvidyānagara, the vast ocean of the jewels of knowledge.
He is the revealer of the great Rāmāyaṇa and the seventy million mantras.
Filled with compassion for the Goddess Śrī, his every desire fulfilled;
the one who fashioned a rain of gold upon the great field of Virūpākṣa;
the author of radiant commentaries on the three Vedas; and the expert in the meaning of ultimate reality.
He was a master in establishing the doctrines determined by the feet of the Blessed Lord;
he was the ordainer of the system of castes and stages of life, a knower of the essence of the Vedas and Agamas,
and the bestower of the glory of the throne of wealth upon the illustrious Karṇāṭa kingdom.
He performed the royal coronation of the illustrious Bukkamahīpāla;
he was the author of commentaries and sub-commentaries on the works of [Śaṅkara] Ācārya;
and he was the illuminator of the commentaries and expositions on all the Upaniṣads.

He who knows the reality of the meaning of all scriptures, who is the Mandara mountain churning the ocean of the science of mantras, who is praised as a crest-jewel among scholars, and who is the author of many treatises;
he who is the rescuer of the Sarasvatī [tradition] and is discerning in distinguishing the essential from the non-essential.
He was the bearer of the burden of establishing the conduct prescribed by the Śruti and Smṛti;
he was the one who dried up the ocean of evil doctrines that lie outside the Vedas and Śāstras;
he was the forest fire to the pride of wicked disputants and a lion to the elephants of opposing factions.
His fame was like the moonlight that brings life, illuminating the quarters of the world;
he was proficient in the eightfold yoga and an expert in Sāṅkhya and Yoga;
his lotus-feet were worshipped by the multitude of sovereign kings.
Endowed with great majesty, he is the abode of noble splendor;
(11) adorned with all titles, foremost among which is "Tiryagāndolikā," he is a possessor of great enjoyments, a great yogi, and the primary refuge of dispassion. (12)
The illustrious and true guru, beginning with the Paramahaṃsa, was a treasury of compassion;
by the power of his asceticism, he had shaken off the irresistible influence of the Kali age,
and through constant meditation on Śiva, he had dried up all his impurities.
Having conquered the sixfold group of enemies, he is capable of uprooting poverty.
(14) He has mastered his senses, speaks the truth, is true to his word, and is firm in his vows.
He is peaceful-minded, enriched by excellent conduct, and ever eager for the welfare of all beings. (15)
One who has accomplished his purpose, whose character is righteous, self-controlled, and free from greed;
one of great intelligence, great heroism, great splendor, and great mind;
a mass of austerity, a mass of knowledge, and an ocean of auspicious qualities.
He was an extractor of the essence of the treatises on ethics, the crest-jewel among the wise;
composed of pure sattva, steadfast, and a knower of the distinctions of place and time;
a treasury of super-sensory knowledge, and skilled in discerning the past and future.
Knowing the divisions of the three qualities (guṇas), initiated into the stage of renunciation (sannyāsa),
enriched by the single staff consisting of knowledge, resplendent in saffron-colored garments,
wearing a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, and with his body smeared with ashes; || 19 ||
With hands resplendent with a rosary of beads, his forehead marked with the triple line (tripuṇḍra),
he was one whose auspicious and great prosperity was the fruit of the penance of the gods upon the earth;
he was ever eager to worship the glorious lotus feet of the Lord who wears the moon on His crest.
One whose mind is attached to the feet of the illustrious Śaṅkara, the Lord of Yogins;
one who is devoted to the worship of Gaṇeśa, the Lord who contains jewels within his womb;
and one whose intention is intent upon the service of the divine throne of Mother Śāradā.
An embodiment of sincere compassion, he has surpassed Bṛhaspati with his wisdom;
he honors the world through true knowledge and bestows joy upon all beings.
He is the abode of graceful gestures of the hand, and is solely intent upon the bliss of Brahman.
Free from possessiveness, free from ego, free from indolence, and free from agitation;
free from anxiety, eternally contented, self-restrained, and free from disease.
(25) He is the Guru, the master of the circle of the earth, established upon the seat of the Guru.
He is independent in all branches of knowledge, an expert in the application of yantras and mantras;
he bestows desired fruits upon the virtuous and is consecrated for the subjugation of the wicked; he is the fulfiller of his promises and the sovereign lord of both punishment and grace.
Worshipped by the world, eternally blissful, bearing the very form of Śaṅkara himself,
and devoted to the preliminary rites (*puraścaryā*) of the great mantra of Mahālakṣmī—
[he was] the great yogi Vidyāraṇya, whose names numbered one hundred and eight.
Whoever recites this constantly shall become a treasury of prosperity and eloquence.
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Śrī Vidyāraṇya.
